body_markdown:
Building mobile applications no longer requires a computer science degree or months of development time. AI app builders have transformed how founders, small business owners, and entrepreneurs bring their ideas to life on iOS and Android devices. Options for[mobile app development](https://floot.com/en/mobile) now include conversational tools, visual builders, and managed platforms that handle backend infrastructure and mobile packaging.


According to Sensor Tower's 2026 State of Mobile report, consumers spent[5.3 trillion hours](https://sensortower.com/blog/state-of-mobile-2026) on mobile apps across iOS and Google Play in 2025. The challenge is choosing a platform with the right AI capabilities, infrastructure, and publishing workflows. This guide compares eight AI app builders for 2027, including platforms that support native app-store publishing and those focused on mobile-friendly web applications.


## **Key Takeaways**


- **MCP integration avoids duplicate AI build-credit billing** : Floot's[MCP connector](https://floot.com/integrations/mcp) lets builders use their existing Claude or ChatGPT subscriptions for connector-based building, with daily building-action limits, metered hosting costs beyond applicable allowances or signup credit, and separate credits for optional AI features and image generation.
- **Mobile publishing on free tiers is rare but valuable** : Floot includes 2 mobile builds per month on its Free plan for early-stage validation. Apple TestFlight is supported on Free with an Apple developer account, while connecting Google Play requires a paid Floot plan.
- **Full-stack infrastructure determines long-term success** : Floot includes managed[Postgres databases](https://floot.com/docs/platform/reliability-and-limits) ,[authentication](https://floot.com/docs/integrations/app-sign-in) , and hosting, reducing the complexity of launching mobile apps that need persistent data.
- **Code ownership affects exit options** : Floot users own their code and data on every plan, although downloading the full project ZIP requires a paid plan. Export options affect migration flexibility.
- **Learning curves vary dramatically** : Visual builders require users to learn component design, workflows, and integrations, while Floot lets you describe what you want in plain language through supported AI assistants.


## **What Makes an AI App Builder Right for Mobile Development**


AI app builders for mobile development serve a fundamentally different purpose than traditional development environments or simple website builders. While website builders focus on static content and basic interactivity, mobile app builders must handle device-specific considerations including push notifications, offline functionality, app store compliance, and native device features.


The core requirements for mobile-capable AI app builders include:


- **Native packaging capabilities** : Converting web applications into installable iOS and Android packages that meet app store requirements
- **Backend infrastructure** : Providing database storage, user authentication, and server-side logic without manual configuration
- **AI-assisted development** : Translating natural language descriptions into functional code across frontend and backend components
- **Publishing workflows** : Managing builds, testing, and submission to Apple App Store and Google Play
- **Scalable hosting** : Supporting applications as they grow from prototype to production traffic levels


Non-technical founders often discover that the AI app builder landscape divides into several categories: conversational builders that work through chat interfaces, visual builders that use drag-and-drop components, and hybrid platforms that combine both approaches. Each category suits different skill levels and project requirements.


## **1. Floot**


[Floot](https://floot.com/) is a full-stack app-building platform with an[MCP connector](https://floot.com/integrations/mcp) that lets users create, edit, and publish applications through supported AI assistants, including Claude, Codex, Cursor, and compatible ChatGPT configurations. The connected AI assistant handles development, while Floot provides managed hosting, databases, authentication, and mobile app packaging. Available building capabilities depend on the AI client's connector permissions.


Floot also offers an optional in-app AI agent that uses separate AI credits.


### **Key Capabilities for Mobile Development**


- **MCP connector integration** : Build apps by describing them in natural language through supported AI assistants, with Floot handling project files, database operations, and deployment. Available actions depend on the connected client's permissions
- **Native mobile packaging** : Convert web applications into installable[iOS and Android shells](https://floot.com/docs/mobile-apps/creating-mobile-apps-in-floot) without requiring a Mac, Xcode, or Android Studio
- **Full-stack infrastructure** : Managed Postgres databases, serverless backend endpoints, file storage, and CDN-backed assets included on all plans
- **Built-in authentication** : Email/password login and brokered Google/Microsoft OAuth sign-in without separate OAuth app registration
- **Store submission support** : Connected builds to TestFlight and Google Play testing tracks, with the platform handling the build process


### **Mobile Publishing Details**


Floot offers mobile app builds on every pricing tier. The Free plan includes[2 monthly builds](https://floot.com/en/pricing) , Pro ($25/month) includes 12 builds, and Power ($100/month) includes unlimited builds. The platform packages web applications into native shells rather than generating separate React Native or Flutter apps, which simplifies the development process while still producing installable applications.


Users receive Android APK downloads through the browser and can connect builds to Apple TestFlight for iOS testing. Final app store submission requires separate developer accounts (Apple Developer Program at $99/year and Google Play registration at $25 one-time), with Floot handling build generation and testing-track uploads but not the final store review process.


### **Why Floot Fits Non-Technical Builders**


Floot combines AI-assisted app development with managed infrastructure, so founders do not need to configure separate services for databases, authentication, storage, and hosting. Users retain ownership of their[code and data](https://floot.com/docs/faqs/code-data-and-exports) on every plan, although downloading the full project ZIP requires a paid plan.


The MCP connector avoids a second Floot AI build-credit bill, although daily building-action limits, hosting usage, and optional AI features still affect overall costs. When building through the connector, AI reasoning runs through the user's connected AI service while Floot meters supported connector operations through building actions: 100/day on Free, 1,000/day on Pro, and 5,000/day on Power.


## **2. Lovable**


### **Primary Focus**


Lovable positions itself as an AI-first application builder with a focus on rapid web MVP generation. The platform uses its own AI system with credit-based billing for development work, offering GitHub integration, a managed backend through Lovable Cloud, and optional connections to external Supabase projects.


### **Key Features**


- **AI-powered generation** : Describe applications in natural language and receive functional code
- **GitHub integration** : Sync projects directly with repositories for version control and developer handoff
- **Managed backend** : Access built-in database and authentication, with an option to connect an external Supabase project
- **Web-first approach** : Primary focus on web applications with responsive design capabilities
- **Credit-based billing** : AI interactions consume credits from monthly allocations


### **App Building Considerations**


Lovable's primary strength lies in web application generation. Mobile app development typically involves progressive web app (PWA) approaches or external tooling for native packaging. The platform's speed in generating initial web interfaces makes it popular for rapid prototyping. The platform maintains a 4.6/5 rating on G2, with review totals changing over time. Credit consumption varies based on project complexity, which some users report makes costs less predictable for larger builds.


## **3. Bolt.new**


### **Primary Focus**


Bolt.new, a product from StackBlitz, provides browser-based application development with AI assistance. The platform emphasizes rapid prototyping directly in the browser without local development environment setup, with support for modern JavaScript frameworks and Expo integration.


### **Key Features**


- **Browser-based development** : Full development environment running in the browser without local installation
- **AI code generation** : Token-based AI assistance for generating and modifying code
- **Instant deployment** : Quick deployment options for sharing prototypes
- **React and framework support** : Works with modern JavaScript frameworks
- **Expo integration** : Mobile development possible through Expo setup


### **App Building Considerations**


Bolt.new handles mobile development through Expo integration, which requires additional configuration beyond web deployment. The platform suits developers comfortable with React Native and Expo workflows who want AI assistance during development. Mobile publishing requires Expo setup and configuration rather than turnkey packaging.


## **4. Replit**


### **Primary Focus**


Replit combines a cloud-based IDE with AI capabilities, offering a complete development environment accessible from any browser. The platform raised $400 million in Series D funding in March 2026, reflecting strong investor interest in AI-assisted development tools.


### **Key Features**


- **Cloud IDE** : Full development environment with terminal access and collaboration features
- **Replit Agent** : AI assistant for code generation and project assistance
- **Built-in hosting** : Deploy applications directly from the development environment
- **Credit system** : AI interactions use credits separate from basic platform access
- **Team collaboration** : Real-time multiplayer coding for team projects


### **App Building Considerations**


Replit supports native mobile development through Replit Agent and Expo. Users can generate applications through natural-language prompts, preview them on physical devices, and follow a guided iOS App Store submission workflow. Apple developer accounts and standard store review are still required. The platform provides the development environment while offering both conversational and code-level interfaces.


## **5. FlutterFlow**


### **Primary Focus**


FlutterFlow takes a visual builder approach to Flutter application development, allowing users to design applications through a drag-and-drop interface that generates real Flutter/Dart code. The platform focuses on creating applications that compile for mobile platforms using Google's Flutter framework.


### **Key Features**


- **Visual Flutter development** : Build Flutter applications through a graphical interface
- **Real code export** : Download Dart/Flutter source code on eligible paid plans
- **Flutter-based mobile output** : Generated applications use Flutter and compile for iOS and Android
- **AI features** : AI-assisted component generation and design suggestions
- **Plugin ecosystem** : Marketplace of pre-built components and integrations


### **App Building Considerations**


FlutterFlow's core value proposition centers on mobile application development using Flutter. Applications compile for iOS and Android, with access to platform features through Flutter's framework. The company announced $25.5 million in Series A funding in 2024, with investors including GV. Applications needing cloud-based data commonly connect to services such as Firebase or Supabase, depending on their requirements.


## **6. Adalo**


### **Primary Focus**


Adalo provides a visual no-code platform for mobile application development. The platform supports native iOS and Android apps alongside web apps through a visual, AI-assisted interface.


### **Key Features**


- **Visual mobile builder** : Drag-and-drop interface for designing mobile screens and flows
- **Built-in relational database** : Included database without external configuration
- **Component marketplace** : More than 50 additional components for extending app functionality
- **Native publishing** : Direct publishing to iOS and Android app stores
- **Ada AI builder** : Generate and refine apps from natural-language descriptions


### **App Building Considerations**


Adalo supports native mobile and web application development, making it an option for non-technical builders focused on publishing across platforms. The built-in database simplifies backend management compared to platforms requiring external integrations. Adalo now offers source-code export as a separately priced service, available by contacting its team.


## **7. Bubble**


### **Primary Focus**


Bubble represents one of the most established no-code platforms, with a focus on complex web applications and business logic. The platform offers sophisticated workflow capabilities and an extensive plugin ecosystem for building data-driven applications.


### **Key Features**


- **Visual web development** : Comprehensive drag-and-drop builder for web applications
- **Workflow engine** : Sophisticated business logic and automation capabilities
- **Plugin ecosystem** : Over 6,000 plugins for extending functionality
- **Built-in database** : Full database management without external services
- **AI agent** : AI-assisted development features for workflow creation


### **App Building Considerations**


Bubble supports both web applications and native iOS and Android development through its mobile builder. Its native mobile capabilities were introduced in public beta in June 2025, with app-store publishing workflows and shared backend functionality for web and mobile apps. The extensive plugin ecosystem and mature workflow engine serve complex application requirements.


## **8. ChatGPT Sites**


### **Primary Focus**


ChatGPT Sites lets users create, preview, publish, and share interactive websites and lightweight applications directly through ChatGPT. It includes hosted web experiences with database and storage capabilities, but it is not positioned as a native iOS or Android app-store publishing platform.


### **Key Features**


- **Conversational website creation** : Build websites and lightweight applications by describing requirements in ChatGPT
- **Built-in hosting** : Publish and share websites without configuring a separate hosting provider
- **Database and storage support** : Create interactive applications that save information and store uploaded files
- **Access controls** : Manage who can access published websites and supported applications
- **ChatGPT integration** : Build and refine projects within ChatGPT's Sites workflow


### **App Building Considerations**


ChatGPT Sites supports web experiences accessible through mobile browsers. However, it does not provide a dedicated native mobile packaging and app-store submission workflow comparable to platforms focused on installable iOS and Android applications.


## **Why Floot Stands Out for Mobile App Development**


For non-technical founders who need applications with saved data, user accounts, and mobile publishing capabilities,[Floot](https://floot.com/) combines full-stack app building with managed infrastructure. Its MCP connector works alongside supported AI assistants, while Floot manages the services needed to run and publish applications.


- **Use your existing AI assistant** : Floot's[MCP connector](https://floot.com/integrations/mcp) supports building through Claude, Codex, Cursor, and compatible ChatGPT configurations. The assistant handles development, with available actions depending on client permissions.
- **Avoid duplicate AI build-credit billing** : Connector-based building uses your existing AI service rather than a separate Floot AI build-credit balance. Daily building-action limits, hosting usage, and optional AI features still apply.
- **Build for mobile without native development tools** : Floot handles native shell packaging and uploads builds to[Apple TestFlight and Google Play](https://floot.com/docs/mobile-apps/publishing-to-app-stores) internal testing through connected developer accounts, without requiring users to operate Xcode or Android Studio. Users complete the final app-store submission and review steps separately.
- **Manage the backend in one place** : Floot includes[managed infrastructure](https://floot.com/docs/platform/reliability-and-limits) with Postgres databases, authentication, serverless endpoints, file storage, and hosting.
- **Start without a paid Floot plan** : Floot's Free plan includes 2 monthly mobile builds and a one-time $3 hosting credit. Paid[pricing plans](https://floot.com/en/pricing) provide higher building-action allowances, additional mobile builds, and recurring hosting allowances. Google Play integration requires a paid Floot plan.


Floot also lets users maintain development continuity by allowing a connected assistant to read existing project files and app state, subject to its permissions. This makes it suitable for founders who want to develop, test, and publish working applications without managing separate backend infrastructure or native build environments.


## **Frequently Asked Questions**


### **Can I build a mobile app with an AI app builder without any coding knowledge?**


Yes, platforms like Floot and Adalo specifically target non-technical builders. Floot lets you describe what you want through a supported AI assistant with the necessary connector permissions. The assistant handles code generation, while Floot manages database infrastructure and mobile packaging. Visual builders like Adalo use drag-and-drop interfaces. More technical platforms like FlutterFlow may require some learning investment even though they provide visual tooling.


### **How do AI app builders handle the backend and hosting for mobile applications?**


This varies significantly by platform. Floot includes managed Postgres databases, serverless endpoints,[authentication](https://floot.com/docs/integrations/app-sign-in) , file storage, and hosting on all plans. FlutterFlow can connect to external backends such as Firebase or Supabase for persistent data. Adalo and Bubble include built-in databases. The choice affects both setup complexity and ongoing costs.


### **Are there any free AI app builders available for mobile app development?**


Several platforms are free to start, with different capabilities. Floot's[Free plan](https://floot.com/en/pricing) includes 100 daily building actions and 2 mobile builds per month, plus a one-time $3 hosting credit at signup rather than a recurring hosting allowance. Apple TestFlight is supported on Free with an Apple developer account, while connecting Google Play requires a paid Floot plan. Adalo offers a free tier for building and testing. Most platforms restrict production features and mobile publishing to paid plans, so evaluate what each free tier includes for your use case.


### **What are the typical costs associated with using an AI app builder for a mobile app?**


Pricing varies by platform and billing terms. The following standard monthly prices were checked on November 4, 2026, before promotional or longer-term billing discounts. Floot Pro costs $25/month with 12 mobile builds and a $10 monthly hosting allowance. Floot Power costs $100/month with unlimited mobile builds and a $25 monthly hosting allowance. FlutterFlow Basic starts at $39/month, while Adalo's Builder plan is listed at $65/month before promotional or longer-term billing discounts. App-store publishing also requires developer accounts, including Apple Developer Program membership ($99/year) and Google Play registration ($25 one-time). Additional hosting, AI subscription, or service charges may apply depending on the platform.


### **How do I publish a mobile app built with an AI app builder to app stores?**


The process depends on your platform. Floot handles[build generation](https://floot.com/docs/mobile-apps/publishing-to-app-stores) and can send connected builds to TestFlight and Google Play testing tracks automatically. You need developer accounts on both platforms, and final app store review and approval happen through Apple and Google directly. Other platforms may require manual export and submission through Expo or native tooling.
